content.text: No MFN or match-my-best-terms mechanic exists anywhere in the document. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: MFN is a direction rule, and the Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation, best-terms, or right-to-match obligation running in Kubient's favour. The commercial terms are set by revenue share in each Exhibit (§5, p0023), with no requirement that AP offer Kubient pricing, revenue splits, or terms no less favourable than those given to other agents or platforms, and no obligation to disclose or match third-party offers. To the contrary, §1 (p0001) expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP remains free to offer Inventory through other agents or sell it to third parties, so AP is under no obligation to channel its best terms to Kubient. The only "no less than" language is the Winning Bid Price floor in the definition at p0014 ("no less than the minimum price that Customer has agreed to accept"), which is a price protection operating in AP's favour and is not an MFN burdening us. This satisfies the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation), so we do not reach the fallback and no redline is warranted.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
